-2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539  MFA No. 100922 of 2024 HC-KAR  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)

The appellant/petitioner filed this appeal being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Court of XII Addl. District Judge and MACT, Belagavi, Sitting at Gokak ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.2283/2021 vide judgment and award dated 21.08.2023.

entities.text: Court of XII Addl. District Judge and MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
2.1.
On 07.09.2021, the petitioner met with an accident while he was travelling on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-04/KC-3298 as a pillion rider.
As a result, the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries.

The petitioner, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 seeking compensation on account of the injuries NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539 HC-KAR sustained in a road traffic accident.

Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
2.2. A notice was issued by the Tribunal to the owner of the motorcycle.
Despite the service of notice, he remained unrepresented, and was placed ex-parte.

2.3. The Insurance Company filed a statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and admitted that the motorcycle was insured by the Insurance Company as of the date of the accident and contented that, the rider of the motorcycle was not possessing a valid and effective driving licence as of the date of the accident.
Hence, on these grounds, prays to dismiss the claim petition.
2.4. The Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings of the parties, framed the relevant issues.

Sri Ramesh S/O Dundappa Koppa vs Imran Pasha S/O Mohameed Shameer on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96915803/
2 2.5.
The petitioner, to substantiate his case, examined himself as PW1, examined the Doctor as PW2 and marked 23 documents as Exs.P1 to P23.

In rebuttal, the NC:
2026:KHC-D:3539 HC-KAR Insurance Company neither led any oral nor documentary evidence.
2.6.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petition in part vide judgment dated 21.08.2023 and awarded a compensation of 5,99,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the petition till its realisation and held the owner and the Insurance Company jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount.
3. The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, filed this appeal seeking an enhancement of compensation.

4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant and the learned counsel for Insurance Company/respondent No.2.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539 HC-KAR 5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submit that, the petitioner is an Agriculturist and earning 20,000/- per month.
He submits that, the petitioner has not produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, the Tribunal could have assessed the notional income as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority ('KSLSA' for short).

The accident is of 2021,
wherein the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at 10,000/- which is on a lower side.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the other heads is also on the lower side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment and submits that, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.

Hence, on this ground,
he prays to dismiss the appeal.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539 HC-KAR 7.
Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
8. The point that would arise for consideration is regarding the quantum of compensation.

9. It is an undisputed fact that the petitioner met with an accident and sustained a grievous injuries,
he has undergone surgery, and the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.
10. To prove the negligence, the petitioner has produced the charge sheet marked as Ex.P8.

The Tribunal, placing reliance on Ex.P8, has rightly recorded a finding that the accident had occurred Sri Ramesh S/O Dundappa Koppa vs Imran Pasha S/O Mohameed Shameer on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96915803/
3 due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text:
Reg. Quantum of compensation:
11.
The petitioner was aged about 49 years as of the date of the accident.
The petitioner contended that, he is an agriculturist and earning an amount of 20,000/- per month.
In support of his contention, the petitioner has not NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539 HC-KAR produced any income proof.
In the absence of income proof, this Court assesses the notional income as per the schedule issued by the KSLSA.
The accident is of 2021.
As per the schedule, the notional income of the petitioner has to be assessed at 14,250/-.
The petitioner was aged about 49 years.

The multiplier applicable to his age group is '13' as per the proposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another1.

entities.text: Sarla Verma (Smt) and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner, to prove the disability, examined the Doctor as PW2, who has deposed that, he has examined the petitioner and issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.P19 and he has opined that the petitioner has sustained the following:
i. Closed Fracture of left tibia & fibula at upper third, ii. Fracture of left clavicle, iii.
Fracture of 3rd, 4th, & 9th ribs on the left side.

He has opined that the petitioner has suffered 30%
disability in relation to the left lower limb and 15% in relation to left upper limb.
The tribunal has assessed the disability at 10% to the whole body, which is on the lower side.
Considering the evidence of PW2 and medical records, this Court reassesses the disability at 15%.

This Court reassesses the compensation under the following heads:
 Amount of Amount of  Compensation Compensation  Sl.
 Particulars awarded by awarded by  No.
 the Tribunal this Court  () ()
 1 Pain and Suffering 20,000 50,000  2 Medical expenses 3,73,059 3,73,059  3 Food, nourishment  5,000 15,000  and conveyance  4 Attendant charges 10,000 15,000
5 Loss of income 57,000

during laid off 20,000  (14,250 x 4)
 period

6 Loss of future 3,33,450  earnings (14,250 x 12 x 13  1,56,000  x 15%)
 7 Loss of amenities 15,000 30,000  Total 5,99,000 8,73,509  Enhanced by this Court 2,74,509  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3539

Sri Ramesh S/O Dundappa Koppa vs Imran Pasha S/O Mohameed Shameer on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96915803/
4 HC-KAR
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of 8,73,509/- as against 5,99,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of 2,74,509/-.

12. In view of the above discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part;
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is hereby modified; iii.
The petitioner is entitled to an enhanced compensation of 2,74,509/- in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realisation; iv.
